text:
ConocoPhillips fell 1.3% today to $134.47, continuing a sharp two-week decline of 11%. The biggest driver appears to be a sharp drop in oil prices: US crude has fallen to $99.64 per barrel while global oil sits at $107.03, both meaningful declines from earlier in the period. Oil companies' profits move directly with the price of crude, so a fall of this magnitude hits their earnings outlook and stock valuations.

The decline also reflects shifting energy politics. Trump's comments on Iran tensions easing "fairly soon" reduce geopolitical risk premiums that had been supporting oil prices, while midterm election results show voter appetite for renewable energy growing—both headwinds for traditional oil producers looking ahead.
